title: Linearity and naturality of completed pullback, direct image, and exchange
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, and put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$ and $P_n=A/\varpi^n$ for a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$, use the completed coefficient sheaf $A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$ and $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $\mathcal C_W$ be its full subcategory of derived $I$-complete objects [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], with the $A$-linear structure [def-weil-linear-category] induced by constant sections of $A_W$.

For every morphism of schemes $u:U\to V$, the canonical map $u^{-1}A_V\to A_U$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Derived module direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] along $u^{-1}A_V\to A_U$ restricts to a functor $D_u=Ru_*:\mathcal C_U\to\mathcal C_V$. Completed pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is a functor $P_u=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}:\mathcal C_V\to\mathcal C_U$. Both functors are additive and $A$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor], and $P_u\dashv D_u$. For a second morphism $v:Z\to U$, the canonical composition isomorphism $P_vP_u\cong P_{u\circ v}$ is natural.

For any cartesian square of schemes $f:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$, $h:Y\to X$, $e:Y\to T$ with $f h=g e$ [sbc-def-base-change-square], these composition comparisons give $\theta:P_hP_f\xrightarrow{\sim}P_eP_g$. Write $\eta_h$ for the unit of $P_h\dashv D_h$ and $\varepsilon_g$ for the counit of $P_g\dashv D_g$. The canonical integral completed exchange is the natural transformation with components
$$
 \alpha_K=D_h(P_e(\varepsilon_{g,K}))\circ D_h(\theta_{D_gK})\circ\eta_{h,P_fD_gK}:
 P_fD_gK\longrightarrow D_hP_eK\qquad(K\in\mathcal C_T).
$$
In particular, for every $a:K\to K'$ in $\mathcal C_T$,
$$D_hP_e(a)\circ\alpha_K=\alpha_{K'}\circ P_fD_g(a).$$
Under the canonical finite-reduction comparisons [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction, prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] and direct-image/derived-limit comparisons [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], this specified mate is the completed exchange obtained from the finite-level exchange transformations. This assertion imposes no smoothness, properness or constructibility hypothesis and asserts no invertibility of $\alpha_K$.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case, clauses (1)-(5); linear and natural-mate refinement for the completed coefficient sheaves, using the comparison of lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence. The linear-functor convention is Tag 09MK, dga.tex, definition-functor-linear-categories. The ringed-topos completed adjunction is also Tag 099K, algebraization.tex, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint; its ideal hypothesis holds because the coefficient map sends the constant section varpi to varpi.

proof.text: Check that the coefficient datum really applies. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a DVR with finite residue field and nonzero uniformizer. It is Noetherian since every ideal is principal. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], every $P_n$ is finite and the quotient transitions are ring maps. The exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A\to P_n\to0$ is a bounded finite-free resolution, so $P_n$ is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Its additive group is finite and therefore torsion. Thus [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] applies at every corner. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] to the inverse system $(P_n)_n$. Its canonical coefficient isomorphisms preserve every constant scalar $a\in A$, commute with reductions, and agree under composition. In particular the four structure maps form a commutative square of ringed topoi, and the ideal generated by $\varpi$ pulls back to the ideal generated by $\varpi$.

source.place: Tag 099N, hypotheses; coefficient checks and canonical coefficient maps

proof.text: Use $L_u=Lu^*$ for ordinary, uncompleted module pullback. The operations and adjunction $L_u\dashv Ru_*$ exist by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. On module sheaves, addition and multiplication of a morphism by a constant $a\in A$ commute with $u^*$ and $u_*$: on sections the latter sends $a\phi$ to $a(u_*\phi)$, and the former sends $(a\phi)(x)\otimes r$ to $a(\phi(x)\otimes r)$. The categories of module sheaves are $A$-linear by these same sectionwise operations; [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] gives the induced linear derived categories and linear localization. Ordinary pullback is exact here and therefore remains linear on the derived category: it preserves the central endomorphism $a1_M$ and is additive. For direct image, choose K-injective representatives $J,J'$ of its two input objects. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every derived morphism between them is a homotopy class of chain maps, and addition and scalar multiplication are represented by addition and scalar multiplication of those maps. Applying the additive, scalar-preserving termwise $u_*$ gives $Ru_*(\phi+\psi)=Ru_*\phi+Ru_*\psi$ and $Ru_*(a\phi)=aRu_*\phi$. This argument uses representatives to compute the already-defined functor, and assumes no linearity of an arbitrary functorial resolution. Full subcategories inherit these Hom-module structures.

source.place: Tag 099N, ordinary operations; Tag 09MK convention; scalar calculation on representatives

proof.text: Write $C_W$ for the Koszul completion functor on the ambient category and $j_M:M\to C_WM$ for its unit. The explicit tensor/product/mapping-fibre construction of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is additive and $A$-linear on chain maps: every component of the induced map is either $\phi\otimes1$ or a product of such maps, so replacing $\phi$ by $a\phi$ multiplies every component by $a$. The same holds for sums. Linear localization from step 2 gives the assertions on derived morphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], $C_WM$ is locally complete and composition with $j_M$ is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(C_WM,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)$ for complete $N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], this local condition agrees with the intrinsic one in the statement, and $C_WM\simeq R\lim_n(M\otimes^L_{A_W}(P_n)_W)$ with its specified unit and strict tower. Finite direct sums of complete objects are complete: the finite direct sum commutes with the products and the two-summand fibre in the displayed model, and the resulting completion unit is the direct sum of their units. Thus the full complete subcategory is additive.

source.place: Tag 099N (2),(5), via Tags 099B and 0A0E; explicit linear reflector

proof.text:
By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], $Ru_*$ takes complete objects to complete objects, so it restricts to $D_u$. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction], $P_u=C_UL_u$ on complete inputs, including its completion comparison, and its values are complete. For $M\in\mathcal C_V$ and $N\in\mathcal C_U$, the ordinary adjunction and the reflector bijection of step 3 give, naturally,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_U}(P_uM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_uM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,Ru_*N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_V}(M,D_uN).$$
This defines $P_u\dashv D_u$. Both functors are additive and $A$-linear by steps 2 and 3, in exactly the sense of [def-weil-linear-functor]. Denote $j_{u,M}:L_uM\to P_uM$ the completion unit. The unit and counit just obtained satisfy $\eta^c_{u,M}=D_u(j_{u,M})\eta^0_{u,M}$ and $\varepsilon^c_{u,N}j_{u,D_uN}=\varepsilon^0_{u,N}$, because both equalities say that the displayed Hom bijections carry an identity to its unit or counit.

For $v:Z\to U$, ordinary module direct images compose by their section formula and the coefficient compatibility in step 1. Their derived direct images compose canonically: a K-injective complex on $Z$ stays K-injective after $v_*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since $v^*$ is exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; thus the same complex computes both successive right derived images and the composite one. This gives $D_uD_v\simeq D_{u\circ v}$ on complete categories. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], $P_vP_u$ is left adjoint to $D_uD_v$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to obtain the canonical natural isomorphism $P_vP_u\simeq P_{u\circ v}$, characterized by carrying the composite unit to the unit for $u\circ v$. Applying this to $fh=ge$ gives $\theta:P_hP_f\simeq P_eP_g$. Write $k^c_{v,u}:P_vP_u\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{u\circ v}$ for this comparison, and $k^0_{v,u}:L_vL_u\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{u\circ v}$ for the inverse of the comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. The precise compatibility needed below is
$$k^c_{v,u,M}j_{v,P_uM}L_v(j_{u,M})=j_{u\circ v,M}k^0_{v,u,M}.$$
To check it, transpose both maps under the ordinary composite adjunction $L_vL_u\dashv R u_*R v_*$. For the left side, the unit formula in step 4 and naturality of the ordinary unit combine the two completion units into the composite completed unit $D_u(\eta^c_{v,P_uM})\eta^c_{u,M}$; applying $D_uD_v(k^c_{v,u,M})$ carries it to $\eta^c_{u\circ v,M}$ by the defining property of $k^c$. The right side transposes to that same unit by step 4 and the ordinary composition comparison. Injectivity of the ordinary adjunction bijection proves the displayed equality. Applying it to the two routes $fh=ge$ gives exactly the compatibility of $\theta$ with the ordinary square comparison and all four completion units.

source.place: Tag 099N (2); natural comparison by composite adjunction and uniqueness

proof.text: Take the mate of $\theta$ under $P_g\dashv D_g$ and $P_h\dashv D_h$, with the other functors $P_f,P_e$. The formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is precisely the displayed formula for $\alpha_K$, and its source and target are $P_fD_gK,D_hP_eK$ in $\mathcal C_X$. Naturality can also be checked without invoking any invertibility: for $a:K\to K'$, counit naturality gives $a\varepsilon_{g,K}=\varepsilon_{g,K'}P_gD_g(a)$; naturality of $\theta$ moves $P_eP_gD_g(a)$ past $\theta_{D_gK}$ to $P_hP_fD_g(a)$; unit naturality then gives $D_hP_hP_fD_g(a)\eta_{h,P_fD_gK}=\eta_{h,P_fD_gK'}P_fD_g(a)$. Applying $D_hP_e$ to the first equality and concatenating the three equalities gives $D_hP_e(a)\alpha_K=\alpha_{K'}P_fD_g(a)$.

We now identify this mate with the finite-level construction as a strict-tower statement. Put $\mathcal R_W(M)=\Delta M\otimes^L_{\Delta A_W}Q_{W,\bullet}$, where $Q_{W,\bullet}=((P_n)_W)_n$. This is the strict reduction functor of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Realize strict towers on the small product sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$; this is a small category in the fixed universe. For this $J$ the object $1$ is terminal, and a map $F_\bullet\to\Delta B$ is uniquely determined by $F_1\to B$: its component at $n$ is $F_n\to F_1\to B$. Thus $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta$. Evaluation is additive and exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so $\Delta$ preserves K-injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. It follows that $\mathscr D_u\Delta K\simeq\Delta Ru_*K$: a K-injective resolution $K\to I$ becomes a K-injective tower resolution, and termwise direct image of $\Delta I$ is $\Delta u_*I$. Pullback commutes with $\Delta$ because the identified-coefficient pullbacks are exact termwise. These comparisons preserve the adjunction maps themselves: for a chain map $t:u^*M\to I$ with K-injective target, its adjunct is $u_*t\circ\eta^0_M$. Applying $\Delta$ gives the same formula with constant towers; the resolution $\Delta I$ just constructed computes the tower derived adjunction. Thus units and counits, and hence their three-factor mates, agree under the constant-tower comparisons.
For evaluation at any $n$, its left adjoint $S_n$ sends a module $B$ to the tower with value $B$ at $m\leq n$, value $0$ at $m>n$, and identity transitions between nonzero terms. A tower map $S_nB\to F_\bullet$ is uniquely its map $B\to F_n$, followed at $m\leq n$ by the transition $F_n\to F_m$. The functor $S_n$ is additive and exact levelwise. Therefore evaluation preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Evaluating the chain-map adjunct formula above, now with an arbitrary tower K-injective target, gives the ordinary derived adjunct formula at $n$. In particular evaluation preserves the units, counits and mates under the direct-image comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits].
Finally, if $P$ is a K-flat resolution with flat terms of $M$, $\Delta P$ is K-flat on the diagram site: its tensor with an acyclic diagram is acyclic at every level by K-flatness of $P$, hence acyclic by levelwise cohomology. Thus $\Delta P\otimes Q_{W,\bullet}$ computes $\mathcal R_W(M)$ and is exactly the strict reduction tower specified above, including transitions. The four topoi morphisms act on diagrams termwise, as follows immediately by evaluating their inverse-image/direct-image adjunction objectwise. Derived module operations and their adjunctions on these ringed sites are available from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] and [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]. Use $\mathscr L_u,\mathscr D_u$ for the operations with ring $\Delta A_W$, and $E^\Delta:\mathscr L_f\mathscr D_g\to\mathscr D_h\mathscr L_e$ for their mate. There are no geometric hypotheses here. The coefficient isomorphisms of step 1 imply $\mathscr L_uQ_{V,\bullet}\cong Q_{U,\bullet}$, with the quotient transitions, using the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

source.place: Tags 099N (4),(5) and 07A7; strict diagram-site realization, not a claim that derived evaluations are faithful

proof.text:
For complete $K$ on $T$ put $M=L_fRg_*K$, $E=L_eK$, $N=Rh_*E$, and $b=\operatorname{Ex}^A_K:M\to N$, the ambient mate of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] with the labels $g,f,h,e$ in the corresponding positions. On the diagram sites define
$$H:\mathcal R_X(M)\longrightarrow\mathscr L_f\mathscr D_g\mathcal R_T(K),\qquad H':\mathcal R_X(N)\longrightarrow\mathscr D_h\mathscr L_e\mathcal R_T(K).$$
Here $H$ is pullback of the projection-formula map for $g$, preceded by the pullback/tensor identification; $H'$ is the projection-formula map for $h$ followed by the pullback/tensor identification for $e$. Use exactly the adjunct-of-counit maps of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on these diagram ringed topoi with the coefficient object $Q_{S,\bullet}$. By step 7 the exchange at $\Delta K$ is $\Delta b$, including its unit, counit and composition factors. Consequently that coherence statement gives the equality
$$H'\mathcal R_X(b)=E^\Delta_{\mathcal R_T(K)}H$$
in the derived category of strict towers. Every evaluation of $H,H'$ is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula], applied to the arbitrary morphisms $g,h$ and the perfect $P_n$ checked in step 1. Evaluations compute derived direct images as in [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Since cohomology of towers is levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], the cones of $H,H'$ are acyclic, so $H,H'$ themselves are isomorphisms. This uses conservativity on objects, not faithfulness on morphisms. Thus the specified strict exchange is $H'\mathcal R_X(b)H^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, on diagram sites; Tag 0944 perfect projection formula

proof.text: Use $E^\Delta$ on the reduction tower as the strict realization of the finite-level exchange after restriction to the ambient $A$-coefficient categories. This specifies the realization by the unit-square-counit construction on diagram sites; it does not characterize a derived tower map just by its evaluations. Check its finite components as follows. For each edge $u:U\to V$ and each $n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $R_W=A_W$, $S_W=(P_n)_W$ and $a_W$ the projection. Step 1 gives precisely its two coefficient isomorphisms and their commutative scalar square. That lemma identifies pullbacks and direct images after restriction, and says explicitly that a map and its adjunct correspond under these comparisons. Inserting the identity into this adjunct equation identifies the units; inserting a counit identifies the counits. The pullback composition comparisons are the termwise canonical ones of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], which commute with restriction. Substitution in the three factors of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] therefore identifies the $n$-th evaluation of $E^\Delta$ with the restriction of the ordinary $(P_n)$-coefficient exchange. The direct-image evaluations used here are those of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] on the ambient $A$-coefficient tower, not a claim about K-injectives for variable-coefficient diagram rings. Naturality of the diagram-site unit, counit and pullback comparison makes these components commute with the quotient transitions; it is the strict mate $E^\Delta$, already constructed in step 7, that supplies their coherent lift. Thus step 8 is a strict projection-formula realization of the finite-level exchange and uses none of the properness or etale-origin hypotheses of the older witness-transported construction.

source.place: Tag 07A7; finite coefficient restriction, adjunct equations, and the specified strict mate realization

proof.text:
Apply the functor $R\lim$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] to step 8 and use the natural comparisons of [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] and [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. The source is identified with $P_fD_gK$ through $R\lim H$; the target is identified with $D_hP_eK$ through $R\lim H'$ and the direct-image/limit comparison. Consequently the finite-level completed exchange is the map
$$\gamma_K:C_XM\xrightarrow{C_X(b)}C_XN\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*C_YE.$$
Here the second arrow is the composite
$$C_XRh_*E\cong R\lim_n\bigl((Rh_*E)\otimes^L(P_n)_X\bigr)\xrightarrow{R\lim\pi_h}R\lim_nRh_*(E\otimes^L(P_n)_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*C_YE.$$
The first and last completion identifications include their units by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]; the middle maps are the specified projection-formula isomorphisms [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula], which apply also when $E$ is not complete. The unit compatibility can be checked from [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]: for the coefficient object $A_X$ the adjunct defining the projection map is the counit, so this projection map is the identity by the adjunction bijection. Naturality for each quotient map $A_X\to(P_n)_X$ therefore identifies the two strict completion-unit maps. Consequently
$$\gamma_Kj_{f,D_gK}=Rh_*(j_{e,K})b.$$
Indeed both sides are induced by the strict quotient maps $M\to\mathcal R_X(M)$ followed by $\mathcal R_X(b)$ and the displayed projection-formula comparison. This is an equality induced by maps of strict towers, so no conclusion is being inferred merely from equality of all finite reductions.

source.place: Tag 099N (3)-(5); apply the strict derived-limit functor to the projection-formula rectangle

proof.text:
Finally $\alpha_K$ has the same property as $\gamma_K$. To see the equality of their composites with $j_{f,D_gK}$, transpose them under the ordinary adjunction $L_h\dashv Rh_*$. By the two unit/counit equations in step 4 and the composition-unit characterization in step 5, the transpose of $\alpha_Kj_{f,D_gK}$ is
$$L_hL_fD_gK\xrightarrow{\theta^0}L_eL_gD_gK\xrightarrow{L_e\varepsilon^0_{g,K}}L_eK\xrightarrow{j_{e,K}}P_eK.$$
This is also the transpose of $Rh_*(j_{e,K})b$ by [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. More explicitly, the compatibility from step 5 is $\theta^c j_h(P_fM)L_hj_f(M)=j_e(P_gM)L_ej_g(M)\theta^0_M$; insert $M=D_gK$, use naturality of $j_e$ to move $\varepsilon_g^c$ to its right, and then use $\varepsilon_g^cj_g(D_gK)=\varepsilon_g^0$. Thus step 10 gives $\alpha_Kj_{f,D_gK}=\gamma_Kj_{f,D_gK}$. The target $D_hP_eK$ is complete by step 4, so the injective part of the reflector Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] implies $\alpha_K=\gamma_K$. This proves the required agreement with the finite-level completed exchange for arbitrary complete $K$. No inverse of a finite-level exchange was used, and there is no properness, smoothness, boundedness, or constructibility assumption in the argument.
